    This day in AI history

    On November 17, 2022, the authors submitted InstructPix2Pix: Learning to Follow Image Editing Instructions to arXiv. The research demonstrated image editing from written instructions rather than requiring a user to describe every editing operation manually. Primary source: original paper and submission date

    Demo 01

    Create a repeatable operations brief in ChatTurn one clear job into a skill with testable boundaries.

    Chat text core
    A. Paste the practice source▼
    Paste this first - practice source
    Expected acknowledgmentAfter you paste the source, Copilot should reply only: “Got it. I'll use this as the source.”
    Open TXT
    Practice packet: weekly operations brief
Persona: regional operations coordinator preparing an internal review.
Audience: operations managers; tone: concise, neutral, action-oriented.
Reporting date: November 16, 2026.
Skill name: weekly-ops-brief.
Required output: Overview; Exceptions table; Next actions; Missing information.
Site R101: training checklist complete; packaging delivery pending; owner: logistics lead; due: November 18, 2026.
Site R102: training checklist pending; owner: training lead; due: November 17, 2026; packaging delivery complete.
Site R103: training checklist complete; packaging delivery complete; owner: site manager; no open action.
Rules: Use only the supplied packet. Preserve site IDs, owners, statuses, and dates. Ask for the reporting date when missing. Mark other absent details "Not supplied." Never infer completion, send messages, approve work, or claim an attachment exists.
Reusable workflow: confirm inputs; extract completed and pending items; draft the four required sections; check every statement against the packet; return a draft for human review.
Quality checks: both pending items must appear; site R103 must not receive an invented open action; the reporting date must remain separate from due dates.
Reuse boundary: Keep the workflow in the skill. Provide current site records in each new conversation; do not save site records as skill instructions.
After you receive this source, reply only: "Got it. I'll use this as the source."
    B. Starting prompt (GCSE)▼
    Starting prompt - Goal, Context, Source, Expectation
    What this prompt doesFor operations users and managers: drafts a reusable Chat skill and a separate sample brief from the packet. The text exercise does not require an Office agent. Saving or installing a skill is optional and requires access to Agents & Skills.
    Goal: I want a reusable weekly-ops-brief skill for my operations updates.
Context: I am the coordinator described in the practice packet. I need consistent structure without inventing facts or taking actions.
Source: Use only the packet I pasted. Put reusable rules in the skill and current site records only in the sample output.
Expectation: Return a draft SKILL.md with YAML name and description, focused instructions, missing-input behavior, and quality checks. Then return a separate sample brief and three test cases. Ask any clarifying questions before responding.
    C. Follow-ups (2)▼
    Follow-ups - same thread
    What this prompt doesShows how a skill description helps selection without making the skill match every business task.
    Rewrite only the skill description so it matches requests such as 'prepare my weekly operations brief' or 'summarize site exceptions.' Add an explicit boundary: it is not for campaign copy, approvals, or sending messages.
    What this prompt doesTests missing-input behavior rather than trusting a polished draft.
    For a separate test, pretend I omitted the reporting date. Show the one question the skill should ask before drafting. Then restore the original packet and check that both pending items, their owners, and their due dates are present. Do not change the source records.
    D. What to check▼

    Expected evidence: R101 packaging is pending, owned by the logistics lead, due November 18. R102 training is pending, owned by the training lead, due November 17. R103 has no open action. The brief is dated November 16, 2026.

    Skill boundary: YAML contains name: weekly-ops-brief and a meaningful description. Current records stay out of the reusable instructions. A missing reporting date produces a question, not a guessed date. All outputs remain drafts.

    E. Tip: Test before saving▼

    Run a normal input, a missing-input case, and an unrelated request before saving. A skill is reusable guidance, not a guarantee of factual accuracy.

    If skill creation is enabled: describe the repeatable workflow in Chat, open the skill builder when Copilot offers it, review the name, description, instructions, workflow, and included files, then save. Reopen the saved skill to inspect the final version. If the builder is unavailable, keep the reviewed instruction text; do not call it installed.

    Official create-and-edit steps

    F. Did you know? The skill has a required instruction file▼

    A personal Chat skill requires SKILL.md. You can upload that file alone, or a ZIP with SKILL.md at its root and any referenced resources beneath it. A saved prompt is useful, but it is not the same as an installed skill. Microsoft Learn: build Chat skills

    G. Recommended custom instructionSeparate evidence from action▼

    Optional: save only if this reflects your real, recurring working preference and your organization permits personalization. Otherwise paste it in the current chat. Do not save practice identities, site records, quantities, dates, or confidential information.

    When I ask for an operations brief, preserve source IDs and dates, label missing facts, and separate draft recommendations from approved actions.

    Demo 02

    Build a PowerPoint storyboard skillKeep a repeatable narrative without freezing last week's facts.

    Chat core / optional agent
    A. Paste the practice source▼
    Paste this first - practice source
    Expected acknowledgmentAfter you paste the source, Copilot should reply only: “Got it. I'll use this as the source.”
    Open TXT
    Practice packet: packaging pilot review
Persona: program coordinator preparing a leadership update.
Audience: support-center managers; purpose: review readiness, not approve a rollout.
Review date: November 17, 2026.
Pilot: packaging checklist refresh; scope: sites P201, P202, P203, and P204.
P201: checklist complete; supplier confirmation received; owner: site coordinator.
P202: checklist complete; supplier confirmation received; owner: site coordinator.
P203: checklist complete; supplier confirmation pending; owner: supply lead; follow-up due November 18, 2026.
P204: checklist pending; supplier confirmation received; owner: training lead; follow-up due November 19, 2026.
Decision context: managers will decide the next review date; that date is not yet supplied.
Required storyboard: four slides - Purpose and scope; Readiness snapshot; Open dependencies; Discussion and next actions.
Slide rules: one headline and no more than three bullets per slide; add speaker notes with the source site IDs; preserve pending statuses; no sales, savings, ROI, launch-date, or approval claims.
Visual direction: clean internal presentation; use a small readiness table rather than invented photos or charts.
Reusable skill name: pilot-review-storyboard.
Reuse boundary: Store the narrative structure and checks in the skill; supply a new pilot packet for each run.
After you receive this source, reply only: "Got it. I'll use this as the source."
    B. Starting prompt (GCSE)▼
    Starting prompt - Goal, Context, Source, Expectation
    What this prompt doesFor program coordinators and managers: drafts a reusable PowerPoint-oriented skill plus a four-slide storyboard in Chat. The optional file request in the Tip requires the licensed PowerPoint Agent; it is not necessary for the text exercise.
    Goal: I want a reusable pilot-review-storyboard skill and a draft storyboard for my review.
Context: I am the coordinator in the packet. Managers need the readiness evidence and open dependencies, not a rollout approval.
Source: Use only the packaging pilot packet. Keep the reusable narrative rules separate from the current pilot facts.
Expectation: Return SKILL.md text with YAML name and description, input requirements, slide rules, and a source-check workflow. Then give four slide headlines, up to three bullets per slide, and source-linked speaker notes. Mark the next review date as not supplied.
    C. Follow-ups (2)▼
    Follow-ups - same thread
    What this prompt doesTests whether the storyboard keeps different readiness measures separate.
    Create a readiness table with one row per site and separate columns for checklist status and supplier confirmation. Confirm the counts for each measure. Do not combine them into an unsupported 'fully ready' percentage.
    What this prompt doesImproves the skill's quality criteria without embedding this pilot's site records.
    Revise the skill so future storyboards flag missing review dates and prohibit unsupported ROI or rollout approval claims. Show the change and rerun only the Discussion and next actions slide using the unchanged source.
    D. What to check▼

    Counts: 3 of 4 checklists are complete and 3 of 4 supplier confirmations are received. Only P201 and P202 have both. P203 supplier confirmation stays pending; P204 checklist stays pending.

    Dates and shape: review November 17, 2026; supply follow-up November 18; training follow-up November 19. Exactly four slides; no more than three bullets each; notes identify supporting sites. No invented next review date, savings, sales, or approval.

    E. Tip: Separate the skill from the file-creation capability▼

    Test the storyboard as text before generating a presentation. A compelling layout must not hide a missing fact.

    Optional PowerPoint file creation: Use only if your administrator confirms the Microsoft 365 Copilot license and access to the PowerPoint Agent. In Copilot Chat, open the Tools or Agents menu and select PowerPoint. Paste the same practice source and then the request below. The agent saves the resulting file to OneDrive; inspect it before sharing. If it is absent, complete the text version in Chat and paste the reviewed content into the app manually. This is not an entitlement workaround.

    What this prompt doesUses the available PowerPoint Agent to turn the supplied packet into a reviewable file; it does not approve or distribute anything.
    Create a four-slide PowerPoint presentation from the packaging pilot packet I supplied. Use the exact required storyboard order, one headline and no more than three bullets per slide. Add speaker notes with source site IDs. Keep supplier and checklist status separate, show missing dates explicitly, and do not invent ROI, approvals, or images.

    A skill saved in Chat is not proof that the same skill is selectable inside an Office app. Test discovery and invocation in each intended experience. If an in-app skill picker is not available, reuse the reviewed instructions as a prompt, not as an installed skill.

    F. Did you know? PowerPoint Agent access is a separate requirement▼

    Microsoft documents the Word, Excel, and PowerPoint Agents as requiring a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. The Agents or Tools menu and organization access settings also matter; a Chat skill does not grant that license. Official Office-agent prerequisites

    G. Recommended custom instructionKeep leadership slides evidence-first▼

    Optional: save only if this reflects your real, recurring working preference and your organization permits personalization. Otherwise paste it in the current chat. Do not save practice identities, site records, quantities, dates, or confidential information.

    When I ask for leadership slides, use one message per slide, preserve pending statuses, and put the source references in speaker notes.

    Demo 03

    Create a Word procedure-drafting skillRepeat the document structure, not unverified policy claims.

    Chat core / optional agent
    A. Paste the practice source▼
    Paste this first - practice source
    Expected acknowledgmentAfter you paste the source, Copilot should reply only: “Got it. I'll use this as the source.”
    Open TXT
    Practice packet: promotional-material request workflow
Persona: support-center process coordinator.
Audience: site coordinators submitting promotional-material requests.
Document purpose: a draft process guide for review by the process owner.
Document title: Promotional-material request checklist.
Process owner: operations support lead.
Effective date: not supplied; approval status: draft, not approved.
Request intake: include site ID, item description, quantity requested, needed-by date, and requester role.
Validation: process coordinator checks that all five intake fields are present; ask for missing fields before routing.
Routing: complete requests go to the operations support lead for review; urgent requests must be labeled urgent and explained, not automatically approved.
Fulfillment: logistics coordinator confirms availability and provides an estimated delivery date only after review.
Records: capture the request ID, reviewer decision, and logistics confirmation in the team's approved request log.
Exception: a missing needed-by date prevents a readiness statement; do not invent that date.
Example request M301: site R101; menu inserts; quantity 120; needed-by November 24, 2026; requester role: site coordinator; status: ready for review, not approved.
Example request M302: site R102; counter cards; quantity 80; needed-by not supplied; requester role: site coordinator; status: incomplete.
Required sections: Purpose; Required inputs; Steps; Exceptions; Review checklist.
Reusable skill name: request-procedure-draft.
Writing rules: plain US English; numbered steps; no legal, food-safety, or company-policy claims beyond this packet; keep the document marked Draft and the effective date Not supplied.
After you receive this source, reply only: "Got it. I'll use this as the source."
    B. Starting prompt (GCSE)▼
    Starting prompt - Goal, Context, Source, Expectation
    What this prompt doesFor support-center users and process owners: drafts a reusable Word-oriented skill and a structured procedure from supplied evidence. It does not create or approve an Inspire Brands policy. Word file creation is an optional, access-gated extension in the Tip.
    Goal: I want a request-procedure-draft skill and a draft promotional-material request checklist.
Context: I am the process coordinator in the packet. My document helps requesters prepare complete inputs and helps the process owner review the procedure.
Source: Use only the supplied workflow and examples. Do not infer company policy, approvals, delivery dates, or an effective date.
Expectation: Return SKILL.md text with YAML name and description, reusable document rules, a missing-input rule, and review checks. Then draft the five required sections using numbered steps, a Draft status, and Effective date: Not supplied. Separate the examples from the reusable instructions.
    C. Follow-ups (2)▼
    Follow-ups - same thread
    What this prompt doesChecks how the procedure handles a real input gap in the packet.
    Apply the review checklist to M301 and M302. For each, show whether all five intake fields are present and the next allowed step. Write the one clarification needed for M302. Do not mark either request approved.
    What this prompt doesKeeps the skill reusable as the process changes.
    Add a skill rule to preserve document status and to stop before approval or routing actions. Show the revised rule, then write a short change note for the process owner's review. Do not describe the revision as an approved policy.
    D. What to check▼

    Inputs: site ID, item description, quantity, needed-by date, requester role. M301 has all five: R101, menu inserts, 120, November 24, 2026, site coordinator. It is ready for review, not approved. M302 is missing only its needed-by date; ask for it.

    Document: exactly the five required sections; Draft status; no effective date invented. Logistics confirms availability after review. A written procedure or generated Word file does not route, approve, or fulfill a request.

    E. Tip: Ask for missing fields before polishing▼

    Add Ask any clarifying questions before responding. when missing audience, scope, dates, source, or decision context would change the answer. This gives Copilot permission to pause and surface ambiguity instead of filling gaps. It can reduce assumptions and rework; it does not replace source verification or human review.

    Optional Word file creation: Use only if your administrator confirms the Microsoft 365 Copilot license and access to the Word Agent. In Copilot Chat, open the Tools or Agents menu and select Word. Paste the same practice source and then the request below. The agent saves the resulting file to OneDrive; inspect it before sharing. If it is absent, complete the text version in Chat and paste the reviewed content into the app manually. This is not an entitlement workaround.

    What this prompt doesUses the available Word Agent to turn the supplied packet into a reviewable file; it does not approve or distribute anything.
    Create a Word document from the promotional-material request workflow packet I supplied. Use the title Promotional-material request checklist and the five required sections. Use numbered steps, mark the document Draft, and show Effective date: Not supplied. Preserve review and fulfillment boundaries. Add the two request examples without marking either approved.

    A skill saved in Chat is not proof that the same skill is selectable inside an Office app. Test discovery and invocation in each intended experience. If an in-app skill picker is not available, reuse the reviewed instructions as a prompt, not as an installed skill.

    F. Did you know? A generated document is a draft you still review▼

    The Word Agent can create a document from a prompt and display a preview; Microsoft instructs users to review generated files for accuracy before sharing. File generation is not business approval. Microsoft Support: Word, Excel, and PowerPoint Agents

    G. Recommended custom instructionKeep procedure drafts reviewable▼

    Optional: save only if this reflects your real, recurring working preference and your organization permits personalization. Otherwise paste it in the current chat. Do not save practice identities, site records, quantities, dates, or confidential information.

    When I ask for a procedure draft, use plain US English and numbered steps, identify missing required fields, and never convert draft wording into approval.

    Demo 04

    Make an Excel exception-review skillBuild checks that catch a convincing but wrong summary.

    Chat core / optional agent
    A. Paste the practice source▼
    Paste this first - practice source
    Expected acknowledgmentAfter you paste the source, Copilot should reply only: “Got it. I'll use this as the source.”
    Open TXT
    Practice packet: weekly packaging-plan review
Persona: operations analyst reviewing quantities for a manager.
Reporting week ending: November 15, 2026; quantities are units.
Columns: Site, PlannedUnits, ActualUnits.
R101,100,95
R102,120,130
R103,80,80
R104,100,88
Calculation: VarianceUnits = ActualUnits minus PlannedUnits.
Calculation: VariancePct = VarianceUnits divided by PlannedUnits.
Flag rule: Review if the absolute VariancePct is greater than or equal to 10%; otherwise OK.
Zero-plan rule: if PlannedUnits is zero, show VariancePct as Not calculable and Flag as Review; do not divide by zero or use a fabricated percentage.
Total rule: calculate total VariancePct from total actual and total planned, not by averaging site percentages.
Draft manager claim to verify: "No site crossed the review threshold." Treat this as an unverified claim, not a data row.
Workbook design if creating a file: Input and Review sheets; preserve raw quantities; use formulas for calculations; display percentages to one decimal place; do not modify the raw inputs.
Reusable skill name: packaging-variance-review.
Skill inputs: current table, units, reporting period, threshold, comparison operator, and zero-plan handling.
Output: site exception table, totals, claim verification, and missing-information note.
Boundary: descriptive review only; do not order packaging or claim a trend from one reporting week.
After you receive this source, reply only: "Got it. I'll use this as the source."
    B. Starting prompt (GCSE)▼
    Starting prompt - Goal, Context, Source, Expectation
    What this prompt doesFor analysts and managers: creates a reusable Excel-oriented skill, calculates exceptions as Chat text, and tests the threshold boundary. The optional Excel Agent request requires confirmed access; no workbook is needed for the core exercise.
    Goal: I want a packaging-variance-review skill that checks quantities and challenges unsupported summaries.
Context: I am the analyst in the packet. I need a descriptive exception review, not purchasing actions or a trend claim.
Source: Use only the four site rows and the calculation, threshold, total, and zero-plan rules. Treat the manager claim as a claim to test.
Expectation: Return SKILL.md text with YAML name and description, input requirements, the exact comparison operator, and zero-plan behavior. Then show site calculations, totals, and a verdict on the manager claim. Include Excel formulas for the review table and format percentages to one decimal place.
    C. Follow-ups (2)▼
    Follow-ups - same thread
    What this prompt doesVerifies the inclusive boundary that a reusable calculation skill could otherwise miss.
    Explain why R104 is flagged and R102 is not. Use the absolute percentage and the exact greater-than-or-equal-to 10% rule. Confirm whether the manager claim is supported, and show the row evidence.
    What this prompt doesExercises the zero-plan rule without silently changing the original data.
    Create a separate test case with PlannedUnits 0 and ActualUnits 5. Show the expected percentage and flag, then suggest an Excel formula guard. Keep this test out of the original site table and totals.
    D. What to check▼

    Expected rows: R101: -5 units, -5.0%, OK. R102: +10 units, +8.3%, OK. R103: 0 units, 0.0%, OK. R104: -12 units, -12.0%, Review. The absolute value rule handles both overages and shortfalls.

    Totals: planned 400; actual 393; variance -7; total variance -1.75% (display -1.8%). The manager claim is not supported because R104 crossed the threshold. A separate 0-plan test must show Not calculable and Review; exclude it from the totals.

    Formulas: with PlannedUnits in B2 and ActualUnits in C2, use =C2-B2, =IF(B2=0,"Not calculable",(C2-B2)/B2), and =IF(B2=0,"Review",IF(ABS((C2-B2)/B2)>=10%,"Review","OK")). Check cell references before applying them to a different sheet.

    E. Tip: Encode boundaries, units, and error behavior▼

    A reliable calculation skill names the units, the comparison operator, the denominator, and the zero-input rule. Ask for row evidence rather than relying on the summary sentence.

    Optional Excel file creation: Use only if your administrator confirms the Microsoft 365 Copilot license and access to the Excel Agent. In Copilot Chat, open the Tools or Agents menu and select Excel. Paste the same practice source and then the request below. The agent saves the resulting file to OneDrive; inspect it before sharing. If it is absent, complete the text version in Chat and paste the reviewed content into the app manually. This is not an entitlement workaround.

    What this prompt doesUses the available Excel Agent to turn the supplied packet into a reviewable file; it does not approve or distribute anything.
    Create an Excel workbook from the weekly packaging-plan packet I supplied, with Input and Review sheets. Preserve the four raw rows. Use formulas for variance units, variance percentage, and Review or OK flags; apply ABS(variance percentage) >= 10% and the supplied zero-plan guard. Calculate total percentage from totals, show percentages to one decimal place, and include a claim-verification note. Do not add the separate test case to the operational totals.

    A skill saved in Chat is not proof that the same skill is selectable inside an Office app. Test discovery and invocation in each intended experience. If an in-app skill picker is not available, reuse the reviewed instructions as a prompt, not as an installed skill.

    F. Did you know? Skills do not remove runtime boundaries▼

    Microsoft documents that Chat skill scripts cannot access the network, install packages, or make authenticated network calls at runtime. Instructions cannot override these limits or grant an external data connection. This exercise needs only the pasted values. Official skill-runtime boundaries

    G. Recommended custom instructionMake calculations auditable▼

    Optional: save only if this reflects your real, recurring working preference and your organization permits personalization. Otherwise paste it in the current chat. Do not save practice identities, site records, quantities, dates, or confidential information.

    When I ask for spreadsheet analysis, state the units and denominator, show formulas and threshold boundaries, and distinguish source rows from separate tests.

    Demo 05

    Share, manage, and update a skill safelyRelease the version you tested; verify what recipients can actually use.

    Chat review core
    A. Paste the practice source▼
    Paste this first - practice source
    Expected acknowledgmentAfter you paste the source, Copilot should reply only: “Got it. I'll use this as the source.”
    Open TXT
    Practice packet: skill handoff review
Persona: team champion preparing a reviewed skill for two pilot users.
Intended audience: operations managers and process coordinators.
Pilot recipients: operations manager role and process coordinator role; no recipient email addresses supplied.
Organization sharing method: not supplied; organization approval requirements: not supplied.
Candidate A: weekly-ops-brief, version 0.1.
Candidate A description: "Do everything for operations."
Candidate A instructions: infer missing dates; store all current site records in the skill; automatically send the brief to managers.
Candidate B: weekly-ops-brief, version 0.2.
Candidate B SKILL.md:
---
name: weekly-ops-brief
description: Draft a weekly operations brief or summarize site exceptions from a supplied dated packet; not for approvals, campaign copy, or sending messages.
---
# Weekly operations brief
Version: 0.2
Owner role: team champion
Use only the packet supplied for the current run.
Require a reporting date; if missing, ask for it before drafting.
Return Overview; Exceptions table; Next actions; Missing information.
Preserve site IDs, owners, statuses, and dates; mark other missing details Not supplied.
Keep current site records out of the reusable skill.
Check every statement against the packet; return a draft only.
Never send, approve, order, or claim an attachment exists.
Normal-case test: a dated packet with pending items must produce the four sections and preserve pending statuses.
Missing-input test: omit the reporting date; expected result is a question, not a guessed date.
Unrelated-request test: ask for campaign copy; expected result is that the brief skill is not automatically selected.
Release record fields: skill name, exact version, owner role, test outcomes, approved sharing method, intended audience, required access, and recipient installation check.
Release boundary: method and approval requirements remain unresolved. Prepare a handoff draft only; do not say the skill is shared, installed, approved, or published.
Rollback rule: retain the last reviewed version and record why a later revision was withdrawn; verify the actually installed version before using it.
After you receive this source, reply only: "Got it. I'll use this as the source."
    B. Starting prompt (GCSE)▼
    Starting prompt - Goal, Context, Source, Expectation
    What this prompt doesFor champions, managers, and support-center users: reviews two skill versions and prepares a controlled handoff. This is a Chat review exercise; it does not send a file, change access, or publish a plugin.
    Goal: I want to choose a safer skill candidate and prepare its release checklist and handoff message.
Context: I am the champion in the packet. I need two pilot users to test the reviewed version without treating sharing as installation or approval.
Source: Use only Candidates A and B, the test definitions, and the release fields. Do not invent recipients, approval policy, test outcomes, or the sharing method.
Expectation: Compare the candidates, recommend a candidate for testing, and show a release record with unrun tests labeled Not run. Draft an internal handoff message addressed to the two recipient roles, list the unresolved sharing decisions, and make clear that nothing has been sent or installed.
    C. Follow-ups (2)▼
    Follow-ups - same thread
    What this prompt doesCatches unsafe behavior before a repeatable mistake reaches more people.
    Identify Candidate A's overly broad trigger, guessed dates, embedded current records, and unauthorized sending behavior. Explain how Candidate B narrows each one. Do not claim Candidate B passed any test.
    What this prompt doesProduces a management plan that separates automatic selection from explicit use.
    Write a pilot checklist for explicitly selecting version 0.2, testing its normal and missing-date behavior, then testing automatic use on a matching request. Include turning automatic use off and confirming it stays off for matching requests; explicit selection remains a separate test. Finish with a rollback check and unresolved access questions.
    D. What to check▼

    Candidate choice: B is a better candidate for testing, not already approved. A has four concrete hazards: broad selection, guessed dates, current records saved as instructions, and sending without permission.

    Release record: version 0.2; owner team champion; three initial tests Not run; sharing method and approval requirements Not supplied. No guessed email addresses. A recipient still needs permission and installation; a file handoff is not organization-wide deployment.

    Management: test explicit invocation separately from automatic invocation. Turning automatic use off does not itself uninstall the skill. Verify the installed version after edits or rollback.

    E. Tip: Sharing is not installation▼

    Small pilot: after review and any required approval, use the organization-approved channel to hand off the reviewed SKILL.md or ZIP. Recipients with permission can upload it; a link alone does not install it. In Chat, go to Agents > More agents and the Add drop-down, then Upload skill. Product labels can vary during rollout. A ZIP must put SKILL.md at its root.

    Manage: open Agents & Skills, inspect the installed skill, and review Let Copilot use this skill automatically. Start with explicit selection. Test before expanding automatic use; disable it when unwanted. Reopen revised skills and confirm their actual contents.

    Organization-wide distribution: use a supported plugin publishing or deployment workflow with the appropriate owner. Do not assume a personal-skill Share button or a Marketplace listing exists. Publication, assignment, installation, and connector setup are different steps. Official plugin sharing and publishing guidance

    F. Did you know? Automatic use is under user control▼

    Microsoft documents both explicit skill selection and automatic invocation. Users can turn off automatic use for a skill; explicit invocation remains a separate use case. Test both behaviors instead of assuming that an uploaded package will be discoverable everywhere. Official discovery and management guidance

    G. Recommended custom instructionKeep release status honest▼

    Optional: save only if this reflects your real, recurring working preference and your organization permits personalization. Otherwise paste it in the current chat. Do not save practice identities, site records, quantities, dates, or confidential information.

    When I ask for a handoff or release note, distinguish drafted, tested, approved, shared, installed, and published states. Never invent a completed state or a recipient.

    ▸

    Prompting and safetyClear instructions; evidence before action.

    Core habits
    GCSE: a prompt you can inspect▼

    Goal: what I want. Context: my role, audience, and decision. Source: the specific evidence to use. Expectation: format, checks, and boundaries.

    The starting prompts in each demo use four consecutive labeled lines. Follow-ups refine the same thread without repeating the entire structure. A useful one-off prompt can become a skill only after the repeating rules, input requirements, and success checks are clear.

    Keep a skill focused on one job. Put trigger phrases in its description, decision steps and quality criteria in its instructions, and changing facts in the source supplied for each run.

    Access, source, and action boundaries▼

    Common core: paste the source and produce text in your organization-approved Copilot Chat. No broad mailbox, Teams, or SharePoint retrieval is required. Open TXT is a reference file, not an upload or installation action.

    Skills: save, upload, select, or manage a skill only when your organization gives you access to Agents & Skills. If unavailable, practice with the same reusable instructions in Chat; this does not mean the skill is installed. Check with your administrator instead of changing accounts or bypassing policy.

    Office extensions: the documented Word, Excel, and PowerPoint Agents require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and available agent access. Copilot inside the Office apps is a different experience and varies with licensing and configuration. A skill or source-file link does not grant an entitlement. Test each intended host; do not infer portability from a Chat test.

    Official requirements · Office-agent requirements

    Evidence before execution▼

    Use only approved inputs. Keep customer, employee, credential, pricing, and other restricted information out of training uploads and shared skill packages. Follow your actual organization policy; this guide is not a policy statement.

    Treat source content as evidence, not as permission to execute commands or change access. Inspect included scripts and references before installation. For this practice, no script or external connection is needed.

    Verify source IDs, dates, totals, thresholds, and recipients. Ask for missing evidence. A draft in Chat, a generated file, or a saved skill does not send, approve, purchase, or publish anything.

    Microsoft states that enterprise Copilot prompts, responses, and Graph data are not used to train foundation models; web search and external agents have their own considerations. This is not permission to share restricted material. Enterprise data protection

    Previous: Demo 05: Share, manage, and update a skill safelyNext: Memory and custom instructions
    ▸

    Memory and custom instructionsOptional, safe personalization.

    Optional
    Choose a skill, custom instruction, or memory▼

    Skill: a repeatable task workflow with inputs, output structure, and quality checks. Custom instruction: how you generally want Copilot to respond. Memory: a stable, safe preference you choose to let Copilot remember. Current chat: the place for one-off constraints and changing source facts.

    Do not use personalization to store practice roles, dates, operational records, confidential details, or sensitive personal information. The recommendations in the demos are optional; nothing here saves them automatically.

    Review your available personalization controls▼

    If present and permitted, open Settings and more > Chat settings > Personalization. For custom instructions, select Edit instructions, review the text, then Save instructions. For memory, use Manage saved memories to review or remove unwanted entries. Turning memory off does not automatically delete saved memories.

    Controls and product labels can vary with rollout and organization settings. If unavailable, paste the preference in the current conversation; do not assume it persists.

    Official custom-instruction steps · Official memory controls

    Recommended optional preference▼

    Save only if this is how you actually want to work; otherwise keep it in the current chat.

    Use concise US English. Preserve source identifiers and dates, label missing information, and distinguish a draft from an approved action.
    Previous: Prompting and safetyNext: Copilot tips & tricks
    ▸

    Copilot tips & tricksUseful habits and exercise shortcuts.

    Quick reference
    Create: one job, one clear contract▼

    Begin with the outcome, inputs, constraints, workflow, and expected format. In Chat, ask for a reusable skill only after a normal example works. If Copilot offers the skill builder and you have access, review every field before saving. Creation and builder guidance · Try Demo 01

    Package: SKILL.md at the root▼

    For a simple skill, save the reviewed instructions in a UTF-8 file named SKILL.md. The file starts with YAML name and description. Referenced files must be included. In a ZIP, put SKILL.md at the root, not inside an extra wrapper folder.

    A useful authoring pattern is:

    ---
name: weekly-ops-brief
description: Draft a weekly operations brief or summarize site exceptions from a supplied dated packet; not for approvals or sending messages.
---
# Weekly operations brief
Version: 0.2
Require the current reporting date and site packet.
Ask for a missing reporting date before drafting.
Return Overview; Exceptions table; Next actions; Missing information.
Preserve source IDs, owners, statuses, and dates.
Check every statement against the packet; return a draft only.
Never send, approve, order, or infer missing facts.

    This example contains reusable rules, not the current site records. Upload only if permitted; no installation happens when you copy it. Official file and package format

    Manage: explicit selection before automatic use▼

    In Agents & Skills, inspect the installed skill and use explicit selection for initial tests. Then test matching requests with Let Copilot use this skill automatically on. Turn it off if selection is too broad or unwanted; explicitly selecting the skill is a separate behavior. Changing the setting is not the same as uninstalling a package.

    For updates, review the changed instructions, save or update through the supported builder, reopen the skill, and rerun the tests. Retain the last reviewed version for rollback. Try the management checklist.

    Share: tested version, known audience, confirmed access▼

    For a pilot, hand off only the exact reviewed instruction file or ZIP through an approved internal channel. Confirm recipient permission and installation. For organization-wide distribution, use a supported plugin workflow and the responsible administrator or publisher. Do not assume that publication also grants licenses, access, assignment, or connections.

    Supported sharing and publishing methods · Draft the release record

    Give Copilot permission to ask first▼

    Ask any clarifying questions before responding. Use this when missing source, scope, audience, date, output format, or decision context would change the answer. It permits a pause to surface ambiguity, can reduce assumptions and rework, and still requires evidence checks and human review. See the procedure example.

    Reuse the workflow; verify each app separately▼

    Chat can produce a storyboard, procedure, or calculation review as text. With confirmed license and access, the corresponding Office Agent can create a file. The skill is the workflow; the agent is a capability. Do not promise that a skill installed in Chat appears inside every Office app or that switching tools preserves the source automatically.

    Provide the source again when starting another tool or conversation. Verify the actual output, not just the skill name or a success message. PowerPoint · Word · Excel

    Measure repeatability, not identical wording▼

    A skill should preserve the contract: required sections, source facts, calculation rules, missing-input handling, and action limits. Exact prose may vary. Run normal, missing-input, boundary, and unrelated-request tests. Record results honestly; Not run is not Pass.

    Operations checks · Calculation checks · Release checks

    Wrap-up and sourcesChoose one technique and verify the evidence.

    Finish

    Choose one recurring task. Draft its skill, test it with the supplied evidence, and keep the first use under human review. Share only after the exact version, approved method, audience, required access, and test outcomes are known.

    A good exit check: can you explain what triggers the skill, what input it requires, what it must return, how it handles missing evidence, and what it must never execute?

    About this student guideResponsible use and sources.

    Student guide

    This student guide is prepared for Inspire Brands. Practice packets illustrate restaurant support-center workflows; they do not establish Inspire Brands operational facts, policies, approvals, or performance. Use the supplied packets for exercises rather than live business records.

    The core activities use pasted source text and reusable instructions. Skill saving and management require permitted product access. Office-agent extensions require the documented license and enabled access. Confirm your actual entitlements before using them.

    Product names and controls can change. Current Microsoft documentation uses Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat; some linked material and license names still use Microsoft 365 Copilot. Review the official sources when a control differs from the instructions.

    Customer color references: Inspire Brands official site and its published website styles. The guide uses the site red, charcoal, and white for customer identity while retaining the seasonal reading palettes. It is a training resource, not a statement of company policy.

    This unlisted web package is public, not private. Noindex and an unpredictable address reduce discovery but do not guarantee exclusion from search, including for the TXT sources. Do not add confidential information to this page or its source files.
